take_homes: Name the crux first: one decision my pricing problem blocks. Give the synthesizer a framework so it has to pick a diagnosis and not average three views.
Default to one agent. Split only for different access, dialect or stance, and check the handoffs, because that is where numbers get lost.
Keep the retrieved sources and the synthesis in files, so the work survives to next week and a teammate could pick it up.

monday.move: Run the crux and three-retriever setup on the usage-pricing pilot: wiki, docs and web into sources/, then a synthesis built on the strategy kernel. Check manually whether the contradictions between the churn article and the Q2 review survived.
monday.who: Me, then one person from my team of fourteen as a second reader.
monday.stop_condition: If the synthesis can't name one diagnosis, or I can't trace its key numbers back to a source file, I don't send it to the pricing working group.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so everyone would keep their own copy.

misconception.why: The synthesis quality came from the framework and the file structure, not from how I phrased a prompt. It's only shaken because the course still hasn't shown me that I can trust the output.

one_line: Good on how to split work across agents and where the handoffs break, but it ends with a briefing nobody has checked, and half the lecture slides say the same thing twice.
